name: Affect Normal Fires
description:
This spell allows the caster to control the intensity and brightness of nonmagical fires within the area of effect.

The caster can affect fires ranging from a small candle or torch up to a bonfire, provided the fire is nonmagical.

The caster may alter all fires within the area simultaneously with a single gesture, choosing one of the following effects:

• Diminish the fire to a dull, smoldering glow equivalent to hot coals
• Increase the fire’s brightness to that of full daylight, doubling its normal illumination radius
• Extinguish the fire completely (this immediately ends the spell)

The spell does not change:

• The rate at which fuel is consumed
• The amount of heat produced
• The damage caused by the fire

The caster may continue to adjust the intensity of affected fires each round while the spell remains active.

This spell has no effect on magical flames, fire-based creatures, or extraplanar fire entities.

name: Alarm
description:
This spell wards a specific area against intrusion by creating an invisible detection field.

The caster defines a cubical area. Once the spell is in place, any creature larger than a normal rat entering the area triggers the alarm.

The caster chooses one of two types of alarm at the time of casting:

• Audible Alarm
  - Produces a loud ringing or clanging sound
  - Clearly audible within a 60-foot radius

• Mental Alarm
  - Sends a silent telepathic warning directly to the caster
  - Functions only if the caster is within 1 mile of the warded area

The caster may designate specific creatures or types of creatures that do not trigger the alarm.

The alarm does not reveal the exact nature, number, or location of intruders—only that the ward has been breached.

name: Armor
description:
This spell creates an invisible field of magical force around the caster that functions as armor.

While the spell is in effect:

• The caster’s base Armor Class becomes 6
• Dexterity adjustments apply normally
• The spell does not stack with worn armor—only the better AC applies

The magical armor is weightless and imposes no movement or casting penalties.

The spell remains in effect for the full duration unless dispelled.

Because the protection is a force effect, it is effective against both corporeal and incorporeal attacks that rely on physical contact.

name: Burning Hands
description:
When this spell is cast, a sheet of flame bursts from the caster’s outstretched hands.

The flames form a fan-shaped arc extending outward from the caster’s fingertips.

All creatures within the area of effect suffer fire damage equal to:

• 1d3 points of damage
• +2 points per caster level

Creatures are allowed a saving throw vs. spell for half damage.

Flammable materials within the area may ignite if they are capable of burning, subject to the DM’s judgment.

The flames do not linger and vanish immediately after the damage is dealt.

name: Cantrip
description:
This spell enables the caster to create a variety of minor magical effects, often used for practice, utility, or entertainment.

Cantrips are limited in power and cannot produce significant combat effects.

Examples of possible effects include:

• Cleaning or soiling small objects
• Lighting or extinguishing small flames such as candles
• Flavoring, warming, or chilling food and drink
• Creating small visual or auditory illusions
• Moving tiny objects short distances

The effects are subtle and cannot inflict damage, significantly alter objects, or duplicate other spells.

The exact result is subject to the DM’s interpretation, but should remain minor and largely cosmetic.

name: Charm Person
description:
This spell affects a single humanoid creature, causing it to regard the caster as a trusted friend and ally.

The target is allowed a saving throw vs. spell to resist the effect. If the saving throw fails, the creature becomes charmed.

A charmed creature:

• Regards the caster as a close and trusted companion
• Will speak freely and offer assistance when reasonable
• Will not obey obviously harmful or suicidal commands

The charm is broken immediately if the caster or allies act in a hostile manner toward the target.

The subject receives additional saving throws over time based on Intelligence:

INT Score | Time Between Saves

3–6 | Every 3 months

7–9 | Every 2 months

10–12 | Every 1 month

13–14 | Every 3 weeks

15–16 | Every 2 weeks

17 | Every 1 week

18 | Every 3 days

A successful saving throw ends the spell immediately.

name: Chill Touch
description:
This spell surrounds the caster’s hand with a pale, necromantic aura of chilling energy.

The caster may make one melee touch attack per round for the duration of the spell.

Each successful touch inflicts:

• 1d4 points of damage to living creatures

If used against undead creatures, the spell instead causes:

• Undead suffer no hit point damage
• The caster inflicts special disruption, often preventing attacks or imposing penalties (DM adjudicated per creature type)

The caster may continue making attacks until the duration expires or all attacks are used.

name: Color Spray
description:
A vivid cone of clashing colors springs forth from the caster’s hand, affecting creatures within the area based on their Hit Dice.

Creatures in the cone are affected as follows:

• 2 HD or less
  - Unconscious
  - Blinded
  - Stunned

• 3–4 HD
  - Blinded
  - Stunned

• 5+ HD
  - Stunned for a brief duration

Creatures are allowed a saving throw vs. spell:

• Success reduces the effect severity or duration

Blindness prevents normal vision, while stun prevents actions and may reduce defenses.

The exact duration of each condition is determined by Hit Dice and DM adjudication, but weaker creatures suffer the longest effects.

name: Comprehend Languages
description:
This spell allows the recipient to understand the spoken or written language of intelligent creatures.

The subject can:

• Comprehend spoken words
• Read written text
• Understand inscriptions, codes, and glyphs (nonmagical)

The spell does not:

• Enable the subject to speak or write the language
• Translate magical writing (such as spellbooks) without additional magic

The caster may instead use the spell on themselves.

The comprehension is literal—idioms, metaphors, and cultural context may still be misunderstood at the DM’s discretion.

name: Dancing Lights
description:
This spell creates up to four glowing lights that resemble torches or lanterns.

The caster may control the lights within range, causing them to:

• Move in any direction at will
• Remain stationary
• Combine into a single, brighter light
• Separate into multiple lights

The lights illuminate an area equivalent to torches or lanterns, depending on their arrangement.

The caster must concentrate to control precise movement; otherwise, the lights remain stationary.

These lights do not produce heat and cannot ignite flammable materials.

They can be used to distract or confuse creatures, though they provide no direct combat effect.

name: Detect Magic
description:
This spell enables the caster to detect the presence of magical auras within the area of effect.

The caster perceives magic in a forward-facing path extending from their position.

Information gained increases with concentration:

• Round 1: Presence or absence of magic
• Round 2: Number of distinct magical auras
• Round 3: Strength and general type of magic (school)

Magical strength depends on the power of the source (item, spell, or creature).

The spell can penetrate barriers, but is blocked by:

• 1 foot of stone
• 1 inch of common metal
• A thin sheet of lead

The caster must face the direction of detection and remain relatively still to concentrate.

name: Detect Undead
description:
This spell reveals the presence of undead creatures within the area of effect.

The caster senses undead in a forward-facing path.

Information gained improves with concentration:

• Round 1: Presence or absence of undead
• Round 2: Number of undead creatures
• Round 3: General strength or relative power

The spell does not reveal exact location, only direction and relative distance.

The detection can penetrate most barriers but is blocked by solid lead or significant magical interference.

Undead that are hidden, invisible, or ethereal are still detected if within range.

name: Erase
description:
This spell removes writings, inscriptions, or magical runes from a surface.

The caster may target:

• Mundane writing (automatically erased)
• Magical writing (saving throw allowed)

If used on magical writing such as a scroll:

• The writing receives a saving throw vs. spell
• If the save fails, the magic is destroyed

The spell can also be used to remove explosive runes or glyphs of warding, though these may trigger if not successfully erased.

The effect is permanent and cannot be reversed except by powerful magic.

name: Feather Fall
description:
This spell causes one or more falling creatures or objects to descend slowly and safely.

The spell affects up to a total weight determined by the caster’s level, typically equivalent to one man-sized creature per level.

Affected targets fall at a greatly reduced speed, taking no damage from the fall.

The spell may be cast instantly in response to a fall, even outside the caster’s normal initiative order, at the DM’s discretion.

The spell does not allow controlled flight—only a slow, drifting descent.

Strong winds or environmental factors may alter the direction of descent.

name: Find Familiar
description:
This spell summons a familiar—an animal that serves as a magical companion to the caster.

The familiar appears after the casting is complete and is chosen by the DM from an appropriate list (such as cat, owl, bat, etc.).

The familiar and caster share a special bond:

• The caster gains heightened senses while the familiar is nearby
• The caster may communicate empathically with the familiar
• The familiar has above-normal Intelligence for its kind

If the familiar dies:

• The caster suffers a shock penalty (typically hit point loss)
• The caster may be weakened or unable to summon another familiar for a period of time

The familiar is loyal but not mindless—it has its own instincts and personality.

Only one familiar may be bound to a caster at a time.

name: Friends
description:
This spell temporarily enhances the caster’s Charisma when dealing with other creatures.

While the spell is active:

• The caster gains a bonus to Charisma (typically +2 to +8, DM determined or randomized)
• The bonus improves reaction adjustments and social interactions

However, once the spell ends:

• Affected creatures realize they were influenced by magic
• Their reactions worsen significantly
• Hostility or resentment may result

The spell is best used in short-term interactions where the caster does not intend to remain afterward.

The spell does not charm or control minds—it only enhances personal appeal.

name: Grease
description:
This spell covers a solid surface or object with a layer of slippery grease.

The caster may target:

• A floor, ground, or surface
• An object such as a weapon

Effects depend on the target:

If cast on a surface:

• Creatures entering the area must make a saving throw vs. spell
• Failure results in slipping and falling
• Movement through the area is reduced and hazardous

If cast on an object:

• The holder must make a saving throw vs. spell
• Failure causes the object to be dropped

The grease is nonflammable and remains for the duration unless removed.

Creatures aware of the hazard may move cautiously, gaining bonuses to their saving throw at the DM’s discretion.

name: Hold Portal
description:
This spell magically holds a door, gate, or similar portal closed.

The portal is held shut as if securely locked and barred.

Effects include:

• Prevents normal opening by physical force
• Bars passage through the portal

However, the spell can be overcome by:

• Creatures with great strength (DM adjudicated)
• A successful knock spell
• Magical or extraplanar force

The spell does not physically damage the portal—it simply prevents it from opening.

Once the duration ends, the portal returns to its normal state.

name: Identify
description:
This spell reveals properties of a magical item.

To cast the spell, the caster must handle the item and often expend material components of value.

Upon completion, the caster learns:

• Whether the item is magical
• The general type of magic involved
• Basic functions of the item

There is a chance that not all properties are revealed in a single casting.

The spell does not automatically reveal:

• Command words
• Curses
• Complete operational details

Repeated castings may be required for full understanding.

The process is mentally taxing and may impose temporary penalties or require rest, depending on DM rulings.

name: Jump
description:
This spell enhances the subject’s ability to leap great distances.

While under the spell’s effect:

• The creature’s jumping distance is greatly increased
• Standing jumps may be tripled
• Running jumps may be doubled or more

The exact distance depends on the creature’s Strength and available movement.

The spell does not grant additional movement—it only enhances jumping capability.

Improper use (such as jumping into hazards) is still dangerous and subject to normal damage rules.

name: Light
description:
This spell creates a bright illumination equivalent to daylight within the area of effect.

The caster may choose to cast the light on:

• An object
• A creature
• A point in space

The light illuminates a 20-foot radius and moves with the object if cast upon one.

If cast on a creature:

• The target may attempt a saving throw vs. spell to avoid being affected
• If failed, the light remains centered on them

The light can be used to:

• Illuminate dark areas
• Blind creatures if cast directly on their eyes (DM adjudication)

The spell counters or dispels darkness of equal or lower level.

The effect is stationary unless attached to a moving object or creature.

name: Magic Missile
description:
This spell creates one or more glowing missiles of magical energy that unerringly strike their target.

The caster gains additional missiles as they increase in level:

• 1 missile at 1st–2nd level
• +1 missile every 2 levels thereafter
• Maximum of 5 missiles

Each missile:

• Automatically hits its target
• Inflicts 1d4 + 1 points of damage

The missiles may be directed at one or multiple targets within range.

The missiles strike simultaneously.

This spell cannot be avoided by normal means, though magical protections (such as shield spells) may negate or block it.

name: Message
description:
This spell allows the caster to send whispered messages to one or more creatures within range.

The caster points toward the intended recipient and whispers a message.

Features include:

• The message travels in a straight line
• It can bend around obstacles to reach the target
• The recipient can reply in a whisper heard only by the caster

The spell functions even if the recipient cannot see the caster, provided the direction is known.

Magical silence or barriers may block the message.

The spell is commonly used for stealth communication or coordination.

name: Mount
description:
This spell summons a riding animal to serve the caster.

The mount typically appears as a strong, well-trained horse or similar creature appropriate to the caster’s environment.

The mount:

• Is obedient and responsive to the caster
• Can carry normal loads and riders
• Has average statistics for its type

The creature is quasi-real and disappears when:

• The duration expires
• It is reduced to 0 hit points

The mount cannot attack unless trained or directed, and is primarily used for travel.

It does not leave behind a body or equipment when it vanishes.

name: Nystul’s Magical Aura
description:
This spell alters the magical aura of an object, causing it to appear magical or nonmagical when detected by spells such as detect magic.

The caster may choose one of the following effects:

• Cause a nonmagical object to radiate a false magical aura
• Mask a magical object so that it appears nonmagical
• Alter the apparent strength or school of an existing magical aura

The spell does not change the actual properties or function of the object—only how it appears to detection magic.

The illusion is convincing to most magical detection unless specifically examined with powerful divination or dispelling effects.

name: Phantasmal Force
description:
This spell creates a visual illusion of an object, creature, or force as imagined by the caster.

The illusion exists only in the minds of those who perceive it and has no physical substance.

The caster may create:

• Creatures
• Objects
• Environmental effects

The illusion cannot:

• Produce real damage
• Exert physical force
• Affect objects directly

Creatures interacting with the illusion may attempt a saving throw vs. spell to disbelieve it.

If disbelieved:

• The illusion fades for that creature
• Others may still perceive it normally

The caster must concentrate to maintain the illusion. If concentration is broken, the spell ends immediately.

Creative use may cause creatures to react as if the illusion were real, at the DM’s discretion.

name: Protection From Evil
description:
This spell creates a magical barrier around the subject that protects against evil creatures.

The protection grants:

• A bonus to Armor Class against attacks from evil creatures
• A bonus to saving throws against effects from evil creatures
• Prevention of bodily contact by summoned or conjured creatures

The barrier prevents enchanted or summoned creatures from touching the protected individual, though ranged or indirect attacks may still function.

The spell does not prevent attacks entirely—it provides defensive advantages and partial protection.

The exact bonuses are determined by standard rules for protection spells.

name: Read Magic
description:
This spell allows the caster to read magical inscriptions and writings.

The caster can decipher:

• Spellbooks
• Scrolls
• Magical runes

Without this spell, magical writing is unintelligible to most characters.

The spell enables the caster to understand the writing sufficiently to:

• Learn spells
• Identify magical inscriptions

Once read, the caster retains knowledge of that writing for future reference without needing to recast the spell.

The spell does not reveal hidden magical effects beyond the writing itself.

name: Shield
description:
This spell creates an invisible barrier of magical force in front of the caster.

The shield provides significant defensive benefits:

• Improves Armor Class against frontal attacks
• Provides greater protection against missile attacks

Additionally:

• Completely negates magic missile attacks directed at the caster

The shield is directional, protecting primarily against attacks from the front and flanks, as determined by the DM.

The barrier moves with the caster and requires no concentration.

name: Shocking Grasp
description:
This spell charges the caster’s hand with electrical energy.

The caster must make a successful melee touch attack to discharge the spell.

On a successful hit:

• The target takes 1d8 points of lightning damage

The attack gains bonuses depending on the target:

• +3 bonus to hit if the target is wearing metal armor
• +2 bonus if the target is composed largely of metal

The charge remains until it is successfully delivered or dissipates under special conditions determined by the DM.

name: Sleep
description:
This spell causes a magical slumber to come upon creatures within the area of effect.

The spell affects a number of creatures based on their Hit Dice:

• 4 HD or less creatures are most susceptible
• Higher HD creatures may be unaffected

The spell affects creatures in order of increasing Hit Dice until the spell’s capacity is reached.

Affected creatures:

• Fall into a deep sleep immediately
• Cannot be awakened by normal noise

Sleeping creatures may be awakened by:

• Physical shaking
• Wounding

The spell does not affect undead or creatures immune to sleep effects.

This spell is extremely effective against groups of weak enemies.

name: Spider Climb
description:
This spell allows the subject to climb vertical surfaces and even traverse ceilings.

While under the spell’s effect:

• The subject can move along walls and ceilings as if walking normally
• Hands remain free for combat or other actions

Movement rate while climbing is reduced compared to normal walking speed.

The subject must maintain contact with the surface and cannot move across gaps without support.

Slippery or unstable surfaces may require checks at the DM’s discretion.

The spell ends immediately if the duration expires, possibly causing a fall.

name: Spook
description:
A spook spell enables the wizard to play upon natural fears to cause the target creature to perceive the spellcaster as someone or something inimical.

• The wizard advances threateningly toward the creature without needing to know what frightens it specifically.
• If the target fails its saving throw vs. spell, it turns and flees at maximum speed, though it retains carried items.
• The creature suffers a saving throw penalty of -1 for every two experience levels of the caster, up to -6 at 12th level.
• A natural roll of 20 on the saving throw automatically succeeds.
• While the caster does not actively pursue, the creature perceives a phantasm chasing it.
• Each round after the initial casting, the creature rolls another saving throw without penalty until it succeeds, breaking the spell.
• The spell affects only creatures with Intelligence 2 or higher; undead are immune.

name: Unseen Servant
description:
This spell creates an invisible, mindless force that performs simple tasks at the caster’s command.

The servant can:

• Fetch and carry items
• Open doors
• Clean, serve, or perform basic labor

Limitations include:

• Cannot attack or defend
• Limited strength (equivalent to a weak human)
• Cannot perform complex or skilled tasks

The servant remains within range of the caster and follows verbal commands.

It cannot be harmed by normal weapons but may be dispelled.

The servant vanishes when the duration expires or if destroyed.

name: Ventriloquism
description:
This spell allows the caster to project their voice to a different location.

The caster can make it seem as though their voice originates from any point within range.

Listeners:

• Hear the voice clearly from the chosen location
• May attempt a saving throw vs. spell to detect the deception

The spell can be used to:

• Distract enemies
• Create confusion
• Simulate sounds or speech from another source

The caster must be able to speak normally for the effect to function.

The illusion affects only sound, not visual perception.

name: Wizard Mark
description:
This spell allows the caster to inscribe a personal magical mark upon an object.

The mark may be:

• Visible or invisible
• Simple or complex in design

The mark is unique to the caster and may serve as identification or a signature.

The inscription:

• Is permanent unless removed by magic such as dispel magic or erase
• Cannot be easily forged or duplicated

The spell is often used to identify possessions, mark territory, or authenticate documents.

The mark itself carries no magical effect beyond identification.

name: Audible Glamer
description:
This spell causes a volume of sound to arise at any point within range. The sound may seem to approach, recede, or remain stationary, as desired by the caster.

The volume of sound depends on the caster’s level. At 1st level, the sound is equivalent to four men. Each additional level doubles the volume (e.g., 2nd level = eight men).

Possible sounds include:

• Talking, singing, shouting
• Walking, marching, or running
• Animal noises or environmental sounds

The volume must remain realistic for the caster’s level:

• A group of rats ≈ eight men
• A roaring lion ≈ 16 men
• A roaring dragon ≥ 24 men

A creature that disbelieves the sound may attempt a saving throw. On success, the sound becomes faint and clearly false, originating from the caster’s direction.

This spell can enhance other illusion spells, such as phantasmal force.

Material Components:

• A bit of wool or a small lump of wax

name: Change Self
description:
This spell allows the caster to alter their appearance, including clothing and equipment.

The caster may appear:

• Up to 1 foot shorter or taller
• Thin, fat, or average build
• As a human, humanoid, or similar bipedal creature

Limitations:

• Cannot duplicate a specific individual
• Does not grant abilities or mannerisms of the chosen form
• Does not change tactile properties (touch reveals the illusion)

The duration is 2d6 rounds plus 2 additional rounds per caster level.

Under certain circumstances, observers may receive a saving throw to disbelieve the illusion, especially if the caster behaves inconsistently with the assumed form.

name: Catapult
description:
This spell allows the caster to launch a single unattended object weighing 3 lbs. or less in a straight line.

The object travels in the chosen direction until it reaches the spell’s limit, then falls to the ground. The object must be:

• Loose or free-standing
• Not held by another creature
• Light enough to move

If used offensively, the caster can hurl the object at a target:

• Attack roll uses caster’s THAC0
• +3 bonus to hit
• Counts as a +3 magical weapon to hit (not for damage)

Damage depends on the object:

• Weapon → normal weapon damage +1
• Small item → 2–3 points
• Large item (2–3 lbs.) → 2–4 points

name: Corpselight
description:
This spell causes dead or undead bodies to glow with a pale radiance. The caster may choose the color:

• White
• Yellow
• Green
• Amber
• Red

The caster may adjust the brightness at will (within 30 feet), ranging from a faint outline to torch-level illumination suitable for reading.

Effects:

• Light is steady and diffuse
• Does not hinder undead in combat
• Does not harm undead creatures

Number of bodies affected:

• Medium → 1 per level
• Small → 2 per level
• Large → 1 per 2 levels
• Huge → 1 per 4 levels

Limitations:

• Cannot affect creatures larger than huge
• Works on material undead (including gaseous forms like wraiths)
• Does not affect non-material undead like ghosts

Material Components:

• The body to be affected
• A pinch of saltpeter
• A bit of phosphorus or a glowworm

Note: Usable by necromancers but not by transmuters.

name: Conjure Spell Component
description:
This spell allows the wizard to teleport desired spell components directly into his hand.

The components must:

• Be naturally occurring
• Be used in spells the caster knows
• Be within the spell’s range
• Be commonly found in the surrounding environment (e.g., twig, feather, firefly, beeswax)

Limitations:

• Components deeper than 10 feet underground or underwater cannot be summoned
• Components cannot exceed a value of 1 gp
• Cannot summon valuable items such as gemstones, metals, or pearls
• Cannot summon manmade or altered items (coins, jewelry, mirrors, cut gems)
• Cannot take components from another creature’s possession

The spell summons three components per caster level. These may be:

• Three different components
• Multiple copies of the same component

Special Case – Animal Components:

Attempting to summon animal body parts (e.g., bat fur) produces unpredictable results. Roll 1d4:

• 1 → Desired component appears
• 2 → Component does not appear
• 3 → The creature is teleported to the caster
• 4 → The caster is teleported to the creature

Restrictions on creatures:

• Only animals with Intelligence 1–4 can be affected
• Humanoids and fantastic creatures (dragons, bugbears, unicorns, etc.) are not affected

The DM should use common sense to determine whether a component is reasonably available within range.

name: Enlarge
description:
This reversible spell causes the instant growth or reduction of a creature or object.

Enlarge Effect:

• Increases size, height, width, and weight by 10% per caster level
• Affects one creature (or unified entity) or one object up to 10 cubic feet per level
• Target must be visible to the caster

Additional effects:

• All carried or worn equipment is enlarged
• Weight, mass, and physical force increase proportionally
• Damage dealt increases proportionally with size
• Magical properties are NOT increased

Examples of effects:

• Weapons deal increased damage based on size multiplier
• Objects become heavier and more durable (e.g., doors, chains)
• A rope becomes longer and thicker

Damage Scaling Example:

• If enlarged to 160% size:
• Damage roll × 1.6 (rounded up)
• Example: 6 damage → 10 damage

The following are NOT affected:

• Hit points
• Armor Class
• Attack rolls
• Magical bonuses

Space limitations:

• If insufficient room exists, growth is limited to available space
• Weak enclosures may burst
• Strong materials prevent further expansion without causing harm

Unwilling targets:

• Receive a saving throw vs. spell
• Success negates the spell

Reduce (Reverse Effect):

• Decreases size by 10% per caster level (minimum 10% of original size)
• Further reductions occur in stages:
  • Feet → inches → fractions of an inch
• The target cannot be reduced to nothing

Example Reduction:

• 16-foot creature reduced by 15th-level caster:
• Reduced to 1.6 feet → then inches → final size ~2.2 inches

Additional notes:

• Shrinking may damage weaker attached materials
• Reduction stops if it would damage the object itself
• Unwilling targets receive a saving throw

Material Component:

• A pinch of powdered iron

name: Fire Burst
description:
This spell causes a nonmagical fire source to erupt in a sudden burst of flame.

The caster must target an existing nonmagical fire, such as:

• Campfire
• Torch or lantern
• Candle

Effect:

• The fire flashes and emits fiery projectiles outward
• All creatures within 10 feet of the fire are affected

Damage:

• 1 point of damage per caster level
• Maximum damage: 10 points

Saving Throw:

• Successful save negates all damage

Limitations:

• The spell only affects nonmagical fires
• No effect if no valid fire source is present

name: Fist of Stone
description:
This spell transforms one of the caster’s hands into a flexible stone fist.

Effect:

• The caster’s chosen hand becomes stone
• The hand remains flexible and usable

Combat Benefits:

• The caster gains effective Strength of 18/00 when using the stone fist
• Can punch, smash, or crush targets

Limitations:

• Strength bonuses only apply when using the stone fist
• No bonus applies when using weapons

Spellcasting Restriction:

• The caster cannot cast spells requiring somatic components while this spell is active

name: Gaze Reflection
description:
This spell creates a shimmering, mirrorlike field of air in front of the caster that moves with him.

Effect:

• Forms a reflective barrier against gaze attacks
• Moves with the caster at all times

Gaze Attack Interaction:

• Any active gaze attack directed at the caster is reflected back at the attacker
• The caster suffers no effects from the gaze

Examples of affected attacks:

• Basilisk petrification gaze
• Vampire charm gaze
• Magical gaze-based spells (e.g., eyebite)

Resolution:

• The attacking creature must save vs. its own gaze effect

Limitations:

• Does not affect normal vision or lighting
• Does not protect against passive gaze effects (e.g., creatures that harm those who look at them, such as a medusa)
• Only blocks active gaze attacks initiated by the attacker

name: Hypnotism
description:
This spell causes the caster’s gestures and droning incantation to entrance creatures, making them susceptible to suggestion.

Effect:

• Affects 1d6 creatures within the area
• Subjects become open to a brief, reasonable suggestion

Suggestion Rules:

• The suggestion must be given after the spell is cast
• It is NOT a spell—only a spoken request
• The caster must speak a language the targets understand

Saving Throw:

• Creatures who succeed are unaffected

Modifiers:

• Wary or hostile creatures: +1 to +3 bonus on saving throw
• If cast on a single creature meeting the caster’s gaze: −2 penalty to saving throw

Additional Effects:

• Affected creatures do not remember being enchanted

Limitations:

• Suggestion must be brief and reasonable
• The spell only creates susceptibility—it does not compel complex or unreasonable actions

name: Hornung’s Guess
description:
This spell provides the caster with an instant and highly accurate estimate of the number of creatures or objects within a visible group.

Effect:

• Instantly estimates the quantity of a group
• Applies to a general class of objects (e.g., trees, soldiers, coins)

Requirements:

• All targets must be within range
• The group as a whole must be visible
• The caster does NOT need to see every individual member

Examples of use:

• Estimating the number of trees in a forest
• Gauging the size of an army
• Assessing treasure hoards

Limitations:

• Cannot estimate hidden or concealed groups
• Cannot isolate subsets within a larger unseen group (e.g., goblins hidden within a forest)

Accuracy:

• The estimate is accurate to the nearest highest factor of ten (rounded up)

Examples:

• 37 → 40
• 439 → 400
• 2,670 → 3,000

Additional Notes:

• Ineffective for very small groups (fewer than 10)
• Commonly used by generals and moneylenders for rapid estimation

name: Know School
description:
This divination allows the caster to determine the magical school specialization of another spellcaster.

Effect:

• Reveals the school of a target wizard
• Works only on specialist mages (e.g., abjurers, conjurers, necromancers)

Limitations:

• No effect on:
  • Priests
  • Non-specialist wizards
  • Creatures without spellcasting ability

Usage:

• Commonly used to verify a wizard’s claimed specialization
• Helpful in identifying magical expertise

Additional Notes:

• The target is unaware of the divination
• Discovery of the spell may cause offense or hostility

name: Lasting Breath
description:
This spell extends the amount of time a creature can hold its breath.

Effect:

• Increases breath-holding duration beyond normal limits
• Applies to one creature per caster level

Base Rule (without spell):

• A character can normally hold their breath for a number of rounds equal to one-third of their Constitution score

Spell Effect:

• The spell’s duration is added to the normal breath-holding time

Duration Details:

• Lasts 1d4 rounds + 1 round per caster level
• The exact duration is secretly rolled by the DM
• The recipient does NOT know when the effect will end

Expiration Effect:

• When the spell ends, the creature must make a Constitution check
• Failure forces the creature to immediately take a breath (per normal rules)

Usage:

• Useful for underwater exploration, drowning hazards, or gas-filled environments

name: Mending
description:
This spell repairs small breaks, tears, or separations in nonmagical objects.

Effect:

• Restores damaged items to their original condition
• Repairs a single break in metal objects
• Rejoins multiple breaks in ceramic or wooden items
• Seals holes in flexible materials (e.g., leather sacks, wineskins)

Examples:

• Broken ring or chain link
• Cracked pottery or wooden tools
• Torn cloth or punctured containers

Limitations:

• Only one break can be repaired in metal objects
• Does NOT restore magical properties
• Cannot repair magical items by itself

Duration Details:

• The repair becomes permanent
• The magical bonding effect fades after 1 turn
• The result cannot be dispelled once completed

Capacity:

• Repairs up to 1 cubic foot of material per caster level

name: Metamorphose Liquids
description:
This spell transmutes one type of liquid into an equal amount of another nonmagical liquid.

Effect:

• Converts one liquid into another (e.g., water, wine, blood, oil, cider)
• The caster must touch the liquid itself, not just its container

Limitations:

• Only nonmagical liquids can be created
• Cannot transform a liquid into a magical liquid

Magical Liquids:

• Receive a saving throw vs. disintegration with a +3 bonus
• Success negates the effect

Poison Interaction:

• Can neutralize poisons in liquid form
• Has no effect on poisons already consumed

Creature Interaction:

• Does not affect living creatures
• Exception: creatures from the Elemental Plane of Water

Elemental Creature Effects:

• Allowed a saving throw vs. spell
• Failure: takes 1d4 damage per caster level
• Success: takes half damage
• Only one creature can be affected per casting

Material Component:

• A drop of the desired liquid
• Must be placed on the caster’s tongue and consumed

Warning:

• Creating poisons with this spell is considered especially dangerous

name: Murdock's Feathery Flyer
description:
Upon casting this spell, a feathery membrane grows under the wizard's arms, extending along his sides to his feet. The membrane appears to merge seamlessly with the caster's skin and clothing.

Effects:

• The caster may glide through the air when jumping from a height
• Horizontal glide distance: 5 feet per 1 foot of elevation
• Movement rate while gliding: 12
• Maneuverability Class: E
• Carrying more than normal weight allowance causes an immediate fall

Expiration:

• When the spell ends, the feathers vanish instantly
• Airborne wizards immediately fall to the ground

Material Component:

• An eagle's feather

name: Nahal's Reckless Dweomer
description:
This spell is the wild mage's ultimate last-resort spell. When cast, the mage releases a sudden flood of wild magical energy in an attempt to shape it into a desired spell effect. The attempt usually fails, but something almost always occurs.

Casting Process:

• The mage announces the spell effect he is attempting to create, including target and conditions
• The mage must know the spell (in his spellbooks) but it need not be memorized
• Upon casting, a burst of magical energy is released
• The actual effect is determined randomly using Table 2: Wild Surge Results
• The caster's level is added to the dice roll

Outcomes:

• Success results in the intended spell effect
• Most outcomes are unexpected and may be beneficial or disastrous
• Casting this spell carries significant risk due to the unpredictable release of energy

name: Patternweave
description:
Patternweave allows the caster to make sense of apparent chaos. The caster can see patterns such as:

• Pottery shards reformed into a whole pot
• Shreds of paper formed into a page
• Scattered parts appearing as a working machine
• Overlapping footprints revealing specific trails

Spell Process:

• The wizard studies tangible random elements (broken glass, paper shreds, intermingled trails) for one round
• DM secretly rolls a saving throw vs. spell for the wizard
• If failed, the spell fails; if successful, the wizard visualizes the pattern
• The caster may attempt to reassemble parts into their original form, requiring another saving throw vs. spell

Restoration Notes:

• Time and quality of restoration depend on complexity
• Only a reasonable copy can be produced
• Works of art restored are worth a small fraction of original value

The material component is a small hand lens, which is not consumed during casting.

name: Scatterspray
description:
Upon casting this spell, the mage can point to any collection of small, unsecured items grouped together within the spell’s range and cause them to fly off in all directions simultaneously.

• The items fly 10 feet in random directions, rebound against the limits of the spell, and bounce around inside the area of effect for one round.
• No less than six items or more than 14 can be affected; items cannot exceed the size of a chicken egg.
• Typical items include coins, marbles, gems, dice, or sling bullets.
• Items in pouches or otherwise restrained are unaffected unless the pouch is open.
• Damage: Small creatures take 1-6 points, Medium creatures 1-4 points, and Large or larger creatures are unharmed. Successful save vs. spells negates the damage.
• Small flying creatures hit must save vs. spells or be grounded for 1-4 turns; Medium or larger flying creatures are unaffected.
• Magical protections such as shield, wall of force, Bigby’s hands, and protection from normal missiles protect creatures within the area.
• The caster is always unharmed.
• Damage assumes hard objects; soft items like eggs or fruit reduce damage by 2 points (min 0).
• Spellcasting is impossible from inside a scatterspray if the caster fails a saving throw vs. spells.

The material components are the items themselves and a flint and steel or tinderbox.

name: Snilloc’s Snowball
description:
This spell creates a mystical snowball in the hand of the caster which can then be thrown immediately against any target within range.

• The snowball hits automatically for 1-3 points of damage, or 1-6 points if used against a fire-using or fire-dwelling opponent.
• The snowball strikes like a magic missile and can be affected and repelled in the same way (e.g., a brooch of shielding or thunderlance provides the same protection).
• It is considered a lesser form of magic missile with longer range at higher levels and can target objects as well as creatures.
• More effective against fiery creatures.

The material component is a chunk of ice or a small bit of ivory.

Note: There are reports of a 2nd-level variant called Snilloc’s Cream Pie with identical effects, though these are unconfirmed.

name: Taunt
description:
A taunt spell enables the caster to jape and jeer effectively at a single type of creature with an Intelligence of 2 or greater.

• The caster need not speak the language of the creatures. His words and sounds have real meaning for the subject creature or creatures, challenging, insulting, and generally irritating and angering them.
• Those failing to save vs. spell rush forth in fury to do battle with the spellcaster.
• All affected creatures attack the spellcaster in melee if physically capable, seeking to use body or hand-held weapons rather than missile weapons or spells.
• Separation from the victim by an impenetrable or uncrossable boundary (wall of fire, chasm, pikemen formation) causes the spell to break.
• If the caster taunts a mixed group, he must choose the type of creature to be affected.
• Creatures commanded by a strong leader might gain a saving throw bonus of +1 to +4 at the DM's discretion.
• If used with a ventriloquism spell, creatures may attack the apparent source depending on intelligence, leader presence, and other factors.

The material component is a slug, hurled at the creatures to be taunted.

name: Tenser's Floating Disc
description:
With this spell, the caster creates the slightly concave, circular plane of force known as Tenser's floating disc.

• The disc is 3 feet in diameter and holds 100 pounds of weight per level of the wizard casting the spell.
• It floats approximately 3 feet above the ground at all times and remains level.
• The disc floats horizontally within its range of 20 yards at the command of the caster, accompanying him at a movement rate of no more than 6.
• If unguided, it maintains a constant interval of 6 feet between itself and the wizard.
• If the spellcaster moves beyond range (moves faster, teleports, or tries to take the disc more than 3 feet from the surface beneath it), or if the spell duration expires, the floating disc winks out of existence, and whatever it was supporting falls.

The material component of the spell is a drop of mercury.

name: Wall of Fog
description:
By casting this spell, the wizard creates a billowing wall of misty vapors in any area within the spell range.

• The wall of fog obscures all sight, normal and infravision, beyond 2 feet.
• The caster may create less vapor if he wishes.
• The wall must be a roughly cubic or rectangular mass, at least 10 feet across in its smallest dimension.
• The misty vapors persist for three or more rounds.
• Duration can be halved by a moderate wind, and the fog can be blown away by a strong wind.

The material component is a pinch of split dried peas.

name: Copy
description:
Copy enables the caster to make a perfect copy of a map, letter, or any other written or drawn document. The caster must have a blank parchment or a book with blank pages of sufficient size to hold the copy. The caster holds the blank object over the object to be copied, then casts the spell; the copy immediately appears on the formerly blank object. The copy is permanent and is a perfect duplicate of the original.

Copy can also be used to copy spells from a new spellbook into the caster's spellbook, assuming the spellbook is large enough to contain the new spells. The caster must first roll to see if he can learn the new spells; if successful, he can cast Copy to instantly copy them into his spellbook.

The material components for this spell are a piece of blank parchment (or a book with blank pages) and a drop of black ink.

name: Corpse Visage
description:
This spell transforms the caster’s face or the face of any creature touched by the caster into the horrifying visage of a rotting corpse. The effect of this illusion is so startling that when it is viewed by opponents, the wizard’s party adds a +2 modifier to their surprise roll.

Creatures with Intelligence of 5 or greater and with 1 Hit Die or less (or who are 1st level or lower) must make a successful saving throw when first viewing Corpse Visage or flee in terror for 1-4 rounds. Corpse Visage does not distinguish between friend and foe, and all who view it are subject to its effects. If the spell is cast upon an unwilling victim, the victim is allowed a saving throw to avoid the effect.

The material component is a rag or piece of cloth taken from a corpse, prepared by dotting it with paints of assorted colors.

name: Detect Disease
description:
Detect Disease reveals to the wizard whether a subject creature or object carries a disease, whether normal or magical. Additionally, there is a 10 percent chance per level of the caster that he is able to identify the exact type of disease.

The material component for this spell is a twig or small branch from any tree.

name: Divining Rod
description:
This spell enables the caster to enchant the branch of a ginkgo or fruit tree to locate a common item that is hidden from view. Unlike locate object, the caster does not need to have a specific mental image of a particular item; rather, he only needs to know the general type of item to locate, such as buried treasure, edible plants, or fresh water. Divining Rod will not locate invisible or magical items, nor will it locate items protected by obscure item or similar spells.

Once the branch is enchanted, the caster holds the branch with both hands. If the desired item is within the range of the spell, the enchanted branch points in the direction of the item and gently pulls the caster along. The spell is not blocked by lead or any other substance. However, if an impenetrable obstacle is reached, such as the ground or a wall, the branch presses against it and stops. If there is no item matching the description within the spell range, the branch does not react, although the caster can move about and continue to search.

The material component for this spell is the branch from a ginkgo tree or a fruit tree, such as peach, apple, or lemon. The branch must be shaped like the letter Y so that the caster can grasp a fork of the branch in each hand.

name: Protection from Hunger and Thirst
description:
When Protection from Hunger and Thirst is cast, the recipient requires no food, water, or nourishment of any kind for the duration of the spell. The recipient can be the caster or anyone he touches. Each day the caster (or the subject of the caster's choice) is under the effect of the spell, he is fully nourished as if they had eaten or drunk normally. At the end of the spell duration, the caster or recipient returns to normal hunger and thirst levels.

The material components for this spell are a small piece of dried meat and a cup of water.

name: Chill
description: This cantrip allows the caster to cause non-living liquid or solid material to become about 40° F. cooler than it was, subject to a minimum temperature of freezing. The chilling effect lasts for an instant, after which the subject warms slowly back to normal temperature. Verbal component is a soft whistling, somatic is a downward-thrust thumb.

name: Clean
description: This cantrip removes heavy soil, dirt, and similar foreign objects from floors, walls, dishes, windows, etc. The subject surfaces are then spotless, but care must be taken in removal of pigments, so usually only one type of material is treated at a time. Verbal component is a low outrush of air, somatic is a circular hand motion.

name: Color
description: This cantrip brings color to an object. It can restore faded hues, tint colored objects, or change hair/skin color. Effect must be renewed every 30 days. Verbal component is a humming, somatic is a back-and-forth or wringing hand motion.

name: Dampen
description: This cantrip permeates the subject area with a fog-like dampness, leaving all materials within it damp. It is useful for various tasks, but makes parchment and similar substances harder to ignite. Verbal component is a low hooting or hummed ditty, somatic is a hand gesture upwards with writhing fingers.

name: Dry
description: This cantrip removes dampness and excess moisture from materials within the area of effect. Useful for cloth, herbs, and cleaning chores. Verbal component is similar to that of the dampen cantrip, and somatic is a two-handed wringing motion.
